Policy Name: Cigna Lumbar Fusion (CMM-609: Lumbar Fusion with Decompression)
Referred Sections: CMM-609.7: Lumbar Fusion (with or without Decompression) Following Failed Lumbar Disc Arthroplasty Surgery

Required findings: Post‑operative imaging demonstrates implant malposition or failure (e.g., subsidence, loosening, infection, dislocation, subluxation, vertebral body fracture, or dislodgement)
Imaging report explicitly describes the above abnormality
Implant failure is directly attributable to the prior lumbar disc arthroplasty at the same level
Medical necessity indications.Source: CMM-609.7 > Failed Lumbar Disc Arthroplasty Implant

Required findings: Greater than six (6) months have elapsed since the prior lumbar total disc arthroplasty at the same level
Post‑operative MRI or CT demonstrates neural structure compression (e.g., retained disc material or recurrent disc herniation)
Patient meets all applicable criteria in the procedure‑specific sections CMM-609.4 (Lumbar Fusion with Decompression) or CMM-609.5 (Lumbar Fusion without Decompression)
Medical necessity indications.Source: CMM-609.7 > Evidence of Neural Structure Compression

Non-Indications: Less than six months elapsed since the original lumbar disc arthroplasty at the same level
Absence of imaging evidence of implant malposition/failure or neural structure compression
Failure to satisfy the criteria outlined in CMM-609.4 or CMM-609.5 when neural compression is the indication
Presence of an intact, well‑positioned disc arthroplasty implant without clinical or radiographic failure
Important criteria & exceptions: A minimum interval of >6 months post‑arthroplasty is required for the neural compression indication
The indication must be evaluated against the specific procedure‑specific sections (CMM-609.4 or CMM-609.5) to confirm eligibility
Both implant failure and neural compression pathways are mutually exclusive; only one set of criteria needs to be met for medical necessity
Documentation required: Operative report of the original lumbar disc arthroplasty including date of surgery and level(s) treated
Post‑operative imaging studies (X‑ray, CT, and/or MRI) demonstrating implant malposition, subsidence, loosening, infection, fracture, dislocation, or neural compression
Radiology report interpreting the imaging findings and confirming the presence of the required abnormality
Clinical note confirming that >6 months have passed since the index arthroplasty

Documentation that the patient meets all required criteria in the applicable procedure‑specific section (CMM-609.4 or CMM-609.5), such as symptom severity, functional limitation, and any prior conservative therapy if stipulated in those sections
